name: application-stat-highlight-band
title: Stat Highlight Band
description: Full-width band of 3-4 headline metrics with labels, separated by dividers rather than individual card borders.
useWhen: Showing a small set of headline numbers (customers, uptime, revenue) as a single cohesive band, e.g. on a landing page or dashboard header.
You want the stats visually unified as one group rather than as separate individual cards.
Each figure is a single static value, not something with a trend or delta to show.
avoidWhen: Each stat needs its own delta/trend indicator or icon — use `stats` for that per-card, richer-context case instead.
You have more than 4 metrics — the band's divider layout gets cramped; split into two rows or a grid instead.
Metrics live inside a data table or list, not a summary band — this component is for a headline strip, not tabular data.
responsiveBehavior: Two columns with horizontal dividers on narrow viewports, switching to a single row with vertical dividers at the sm breakpoint — never both directions of divider at once.
accessibility: Stats use a <dl> so each value has a programmatic label (the metric name), not just visual proximity to its heading.
Values use the font's default proportional figures, not tabular-nums, since this is a set of large standalone headline numbers rather than a column that needs vertical alignment.
Dividers are drawn with divide-x/divide-y utilities rather than a border-per-cell, avoiding doubled borders between adjacent stats.

variants.title: Stat Highlight Band
variants.description: Four metrics (Customers, Countries, Uptime, Transactions) in one divided band.
accessibility: The column-count Tailwind class is chosen from a static lookup keyed by stat count (3 or 4), never built via string interpolation, so Tailwind's content scanner reliably picks it up.

variants.title: Stat Highlight Band (Dark)
variants.description: Stat highlight band adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Divider and label colors are tuned to remain visible but recessive against the dark surface, keeping the value as the primary read.
